definition: Gemini is a family of multimodal large language models (LLMs) developed by Google DeepMind, and the successor to LaMDA and PaLM 2.
details: Comprising Gemini Pro, Gemini Deep Think, Gemini Flash, and Gemini Flash Lite, it was announced on December 6, 2023. It powers the Gemini chatbot, and was named after the Gemini zodiac sign.

explainer.lead: Gemini is Google DeepMind’s family of multimodal large language models, designed to work with text, images, audio, video, and computer code. Its variants span complex cloud-based tasks and on-device processing, and it powers products including the Gemini chatbot.

tiers.eli5: It's a model that can look at pictures, listen to audio, and read text, rather than only reading words.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers pick among the family's variants for different cost and capability needs and use it to power the Gemini chatbot. A pitfall is assuming details are public: size and architecture beyond the announced facts are undisclosed.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, Gemini is a multimodal LLM family comprising Gemini Pro, Gemini Deep Think, Gemini Flash, and Gemini Flash Lite; it was designed to process multiple data types simultaneously. Public technical limits are not disclosed.

components.name: Gemini Ultra

components.name: Gemini Pro
components.detail: The general-purpose Gemini 1.0 model designed for a wide range of tasks.

components.name: Gemini Nano
components.detail: The Gemini 1.0 model designed for on-device tasks.

components.name: Gemini 1.5
components.detail: An update using a mixture-of-experts architecture and a one-million-token context window.

flow: Text, images, audio, video, or computer code can serve as multimodal input.
A model variant handles the input according to the task and deployment setting.
Ultra targets complex tasks, Pro covers broad cloud and product uses, and Nano runs on devices.
For example, Bard used Pro at launch, while the Pixel 8 Pro used Nano.
explainer.origin: Google introduced Gemini as a PaLM 2 successor at Google I/O on May 10, 2023, and Sundar Pichai and Demis Hassabis announced Gemini 1.0 on December 6, 2023. It was developed through collaboration between DeepMind and Google Brain, which had merged as Google DeepMind. Its name references twins, symbolizing that merger, as well as NASA’s Project Gemini.
explainer.lineage: Gemini succeeded LaMDA and PaLM 2. Gemini 1.0 was followed by Gemini 1.5 in February 2024 and Gemini 2.0 Flash Experimental in December 2024; Google also introduced the smaller Gemma range and later based Gemini Robotics on the Gemini 2.0 family.
explainer.whyItMatters: Gemini brought Google DeepMind’s language-model work into a multimodal family spanning cloud services and consumer devices. Its reported MMLU result made Ultra a prominent benchmark milestone, while integrations across chat, phones, developer platforms, and robotics show the family’s broad role.
